plan.notes: Source: VCU Academic Bulletin (bulletin.vcu.edu), program page 'Computer Science, Bachelor of Science (B.S.) with a concentration in cybersecurity', https://bulletin.vcu.edu/undergraduate/engineering/computer-science/computer-science-bs-concentration-cybersecurity/ ; transcribed from the official 'Recommended course sequence/plan of study' table on that page. Catalog year: 2026-2027. Note: as of the fetch date (2026-09-30) the bulletin still labels itself the preliminary/launch version of the 2026-2027 edition; the concentration's curriculum content is fully published and its official sample plan is the source of this transcription. Transcription method: every row of the official sample plan transcribed 1:1, in order; choice slots represent official 'or'/'select' rows and use choice:true with descriptive placeholder codes. No courses invented. Credit accounting: term hours match the bulletin exactly (17/14/14/16/17/15/15/12 = 120). Caveats: (1) Natural science option is 3-5 credits officially (CHEM 101+CHEZ 101 = 4, PHYS 207+PHYZ 207 = 5, BIOL 151+BIOZ 151 = 4); 4 credits recorded so the plan totals the official 120 - choosing the 5-credit physics option makes the degree 121 credits. (2) Spring Year 4 open electives are 2-3 credits officially; 3 recorded to reach 120. (3) Based on the VCU Computer Science Placement Test, students may be required to take CMSC 254 (it can count as an elective); MATH 200 entry is via MATH 151 (min C) or a satisfactory score on the VCU Mathematics Placement Test. (4) Students must earn a minimum grade of C in all computer science courses to graduate; CMSC 254 enrollment is restricted to College of Engineering majors. (5) Prerequisite chains are from the official bulletin course pages (azcourses): CMSC 255 accepts BNFO 201, CLSE 115, CMSC 210, CMSC 254, EGRB 215, or INFO 202 - CMSC 254 recorded as the in-sequence path; CMSC 256/302 also accept MATH 151 or MATH 201 or calculus-level placement - MATH 200 recorded as the in-plan path. (6) Bulletin sample plan lists STAT 212 or STAT 210, but the official STAT course page states STAT 210 is not open to computer science majors, so CS students take STAT 212. (7) CMSC 441/451/442/452 are the senior capstone sequence; CMSC 442/452 require CMSC 408, CMSC 441 and CMSC 451. (8) Concentration requirement beyond the core: CMSC 413 Introduction to Cybersecurity (prereq CMSC 357), CMSC 414 Computer and Network Security (prereq CMSC 357), CMSC 415 Introduction to Cryptography (prereq CMSC 401). The cybersecurity sample plan places CMSC 440 Data Communication and Networking in Spring Year 4 and has no CMSC upper-level elective slots; both senior-year blank rows are officially 'Open electives'.
